newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Five hurt in fire at Bahrain cooking oil plant.
newsitem.headline: Five hurt in fire at Bahrain cooking oil plant.

text.p: Five people were slightly hurt when a fire broke out at a cooking oil plant in Bahrain, local newspapers reported on Monday.
The blaze, at a plant owned by Saudi Arabian company Savola, started last night and spread to several units at the site, a government official said.
"The fire spread to other production parts of the plant which was damaged," the official said, without giving further details.
Savola Bahrain is 60 percent owned by the Jeddah-based Savola Company of Saudi Arabia, the main supplier of cooking oil in the kingdom.

Bahraini newspapers said on Monday five people were slightly wounded and that the fire spread to a nearby factory belonging to Omega chemical industries on the small island of Sitra, two km (one mile) south of the capital Manama.
Witnesses said firemen brought the blaze under control. The cause of the fire was not immediately known, they said.
Savola, traded on the Saudi market, is the main investor in a joint Saudi-British sugar refinery being built in Jeddah at a cost of $119 million.
